C3. Node QC proves operation logic but not that a browser can run it, so the operations are now bundled and executed inside Chromium and WebKit against the same output contract, and the image editor and PDF page tools are driven through their real UI. All 615 operations and all 13 UI destinations pass in both engines: no tool needed removing. Three real problems were found and fixed: the e2e suite had been attaching to another project's dev server on port 3000, so all 628 route smoke tests were passing against an unrelated app (now its own port, production build, plus a global setup that refuses a foreign server); WebKit returns a PNG for a canvas WebP request, which the image editor and optimizer treated as failure, leaving both dead on that engine at their default WebP setting (they now keep the produced blob, name the file for its real format and show it on the receipt); and two legacy specs fed the AI background remover a flat single-colour square with no subject, which the model correctly refused.

Compress PDF is the most-searched PDF tool and the one competitors gate hardest; it now runs with no upload at /pdf/compress. A lossless pass rewrites with object streams and can clear document metadata; an image pass re-encodes embedded JPEGs and downsamples oversized ones. Only images that can be rewritten without changing how the page renders are touched (single DCTDecode filter, 8 bpc, DeviceRGB or DeviceGray, no custom decode array); CMYK, indexed and ICC images are left alone. If the output is not smaller the original bytes are returned and the receipt says so. Figures are measured on a noise-heavy 3-page photo PDF, close to the worst case for any codec. The e2e specs save the real download and reopen it with pdf-lib rather than trusting the on-screen receipt. The /guides/pdf-compress-pdf guide pointed at a control the page tool never had and now points at the tool that runs it.

The Worker re-rendered every page on every request (no edge cache, no prerendered HTML, Cache-Control: no-store), which produced 1,316 exceededResources 503s in the 2026-09-16T21:00Z hour. Added the @vinext/cloudflare KV data cache adapter (MIT, cloudflare/vinext, pinned beta.7 because beta.8 requires vinext >= beta.10 and we run beta.9) with a new VINEXT_KV_CACHE namespace, plus one root-layout revalidate=86400 so every route inherits it without editing any Antigravity-owned file. Pages now render once, persist in KV, and return s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=31449600. Build-time prerender was measured and rejected: 3.0MB gzip for 140 routes and 11.9MB for all 627, over Cloudflare's 10MB script limit, for no gain once KV fills; the bundle stays at 0.96MB. Verified X-Vinext-Cache HIT on /, a guide, a blog post, a template and a category hub, with 200/404/308 behaviour unchanged. Not deployed.

C4 release. Shipped the truth clean-up (C1-C3 and A1-A4), the new client-side PDF compressor, and another session's KV-backed ISR cache. Cleared the release gate first by taking wrangler to 4.133.0 with the matching vite-plugin and workers-types, which removed four high-severity sharp/libheif advisories reached through miniflare; SBOM regenerated to match. Verified live after deploy: /pdf/compress and /guides/pdf-compress-pdf return 200, the removed pages (/video/compress, /image/ocr, /roadmap, the video blog article) return 404, the video hub and sql-visualizer redirect, sitemap is 626 URLs, llms.txt lists 537 working tools, pages serve x-vinext-cache HIT with s-maxage=86400, and the compressor spec passes against the live site in Chromium and WebKit.

Filling and signing a PDF is the paid-tier feature at every competitor and the one people most often hand to a stranger's server. /pdf/sign now does it in the tab. inspectPdfForm reads the real AcroForm and reports each field's kind and the options a choice field accepts, so the UI cannot offer a value the file would reject. fillPdfForm writes the values, stamps an optional PNG signature and can flatten; placement converts the UI's top-left coordinates to the PDF's bottom-left origin against the real page height so the mark lands where it was dropped on any page size. Two limits are stated on the page rather than implied away: this draws a signature and does not certify one (no certificate, no audit trail), and drawing needs a pointer with no keyboard equivalent yet. The e2e specs save the real download and reopen it with pdf-lib to read back the written values, assert flattening actually removes the form, and cover a PDF with no fields at all. /guides/pdf-sign-pdf and /guides/pdf-fill-pdf-form pointed at a ?tool= control the page tool never had and now point at the tool that runs them. Committed, not deployed.
